label: 1-2 steps after an early letter o (input phase / delimiter)
explanation: Fires in the original-input phase (and on <DEL>) on the one or two steps right after the token o was input, when that happens early in the sequence (t <= 5). The current token itself does not matter. Activation is strongest on the step right after o (prev_tok=o has 43% rate and 69% of mass; typical 0.5-1.0 of max) and weaker two steps after (about 0.3-0.4). The largest activations come when o appeared twice in a row early (e.g. o o g -> 1.0 on g). Activation fades with position, and an o just before <DEL> or late in a long sequence often gives nothing. It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.4% of mass), and it is silent at t=0. The remaining weak activations (lowest quartile, around 0.1 of max) sit three steps after o or on scattered tokens.

issues: Minor numeric misstatement: the explanation says prev_tok=o has a '43% firing rate'. On dev, prev_tok=o & phase<2 & t<6 has precision 0.944, so the firing rate when the condition holds is about 94%. It covers 51% of active steps and 68% of activation mass. Without the t limit, precision is 0.726 and mass recall is 0.69, which matches the stated 69% mass share. The '43%' looks mislabeled, not a real gap.

The hard t<6 cutoff is a soft boundary. Several test misses come from an o input at t=4-5 that still fires at t=6-7, e.g. 'b f f o [2:0.45] [u:0.30]' and 'y l a o [c:0.53] [<DEL>:0.40]'. Relaxing to t<7 (F1 0.833) or using t<7 for prev_tok only (F1 0.851) lowers test F1 below the original 0.869, so the original cutoff is the best tradeoff found.
False positives are mostly two-steps-after-o cases (prev2_tok=o precision 0.83, versus 0.94 for prev_tok=o) and o just before <DEL>. The explanation already says this.

Verified claims: zero activation at t=0. The copy phase holds 0.4% of activation mass. o o followed by a token fires almost always (precision 0.999). Three-steps-after-o activations are rare and weak (rel_tok(3)=o recall 0.077, mass 0.074). Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.893, R 0.846, F1 0.869, mass recall 0.945). The missed activations hold only 5.5% of mass and are concentrated in the lowest activation quartile.
